policy: Exact AST baseline of forbidden-direction imports. A new edge, a grown edge count, a stale entry or a missing reason fails lint via scripts/check_layer_directions.py. Removing an edge requires a reviewed slice with characterization tests; the allowlist is intentionally not auto-fixable.

decisions.infrastructure>application: FORBIDDEN. The application facade owns adapters, not the reverse. A contract belongs to its consumer; infrastructure may not reach into application. Historical edges are inventoried here, not approved as a design.
decisions.ui>presentation: FORBIDDEN (current baseline: 0). Presentation is the composition shell and may mount UI leaf widgets; shared primitives (segment_labels, segment_label_anchors, ui_metrics, cine_phase_geometry, cine_phase_strip) live in ui/ so leaf widgets never reach back into presentation (#481).
decisions.ui>infrastructure: FORBIDDEN (current baseline: 0), consistent with the presentation->infrastructure ratchet (#307): leaf widgets go through application facades (localization, diagnostics, profile_settings), not directly to adapters (#481).
decisions.constructor>infrastructure: FORBIDDEN (current baseline: 0). Reference constructor widgets and exporters route localization and safe error categorisation through application.localization and application.diagnostics (#481).
decisions.constructor>presentation: FORBIDDEN FOR NEW EDGES; FROZEN AT 14 IMPORTS (#481). Owner decision (#481, option a): constructor is an in-app desktop feature subpackage logically belonging under presentation/reference_constructor/ (opened from MainWindow / ReferenceWindow and intentionally sharing dark_theme, icon_loader, and styled_dialogs). Existing theme/icon/dialog edges are frozen here until physical package relocation so no unreviewed coupling can accumulate.
decisions.presentation>ui: ALLOWED. presentation composes ui leaf widgets and shared UI primitives (strain_window, cine_phase_strip, segment_labels, ui_metrics).
decisions.presentation>constructor: ALLOWED. presentation/ase_reference_dialog.py and reference_window.py open the in-app reference constructor dialog.
decisions.application>infrastructure: ALLOWED. The application facade depends on its adapters; this is the direction the architecture intends.
decisions.infrastructure>domain: ALLOWED. Adapters use domain contracts and value objects.
decisions.ui>domain: ALLOWED. Leaf widgets use domain value objects and timeline services.
decisions.constructor>domain: ALLOWED. Reference constructor reads domain validation/reference contracts.
decisions.contract_ownership: application/preferences_contract.py remains in application. It is NOT moved to domain/ports.py: the consumer (application) owns the contract.
decisions.constructor: DECIDED (#481, option a): constructor is an in-app presentation feature package (target location: presentation/reference_constructor/), not an independent CLI/library layer. All constructor->infrastructure edges were eliminated via application.localization and application.diagnostics (15 -> 0), and the 14 shared presentation edges (dark_theme, icon_loader, styled_dialogs) are frozen in entries below.

entries.reason: The DIMSE adapter reads the consumer-owned, read-only transport_policy. Reversing this edge needs an application-side port decision; no mechanical move of the policy.
Measurement persistence reuses an application dataclass as its storage DTO. The DTO stays with its consumer until a storage-owned schema is designed and characterized.
The Orthanc adapter reads the same consumer-owned transport_policy as the DIMSE adapter; one contract, two adapters, no new edge.

The factory wires query/retrieve service constructors; the type-only and lazy imports avoid a runtime cycle but still point the wrong way. Splitting it requires characterization tests for client construction.
Server settings storage reads the consumer-owned transport_policy. This is the same historical edge as the two clients, not a new dependency.

Three names are imported from the application-owned preferences_contract (display scale). The contract stays in application: its consumer owns it, and moving it to domain/ports.py without an owner argument is explicitly out of scope.
The persistent preferences adapter reads the same application-owned preferences_contract. Same ownership decision as ui_scale.py; no mechanical move to domain/ports.py.
In-app reference constructor dialog shares presentation theme palette, SVG icon loader, and styled save dialog per #481 ownership decision (option a: presentation feature subpackage).
Reference constructor workspace uses presentation styled open/save file dialogs for YAML import and PDF/HTML export (#481, option a).
Constructor how-to dialog applies the active presentation theme palette (#481, option a).
Constructor image editor uses the active presentation theme tokens/palette and styled multi-file open dialog (#481, option a).
Constructor metadata editor applies the active presentation theme palette (#481, option a).
Constructor parameter table editor applies the active presentation theme tokens/palette (#481, option a).
Constructor pathology editor applies the active presentation theme tokens/palette (#481, option a).
Constructor topic editor applies the active presentation theme tokens/palette (#481, option a).
Constructor live preview applies the active presentation theme palette (#481, option a).

facade_reexports.reason: Cross-cutting stateless diagnostics/logging functions (#307). Zero infrastructure types are re-exported; wrapping log_boundary_failure and profiled would add per-call indirection on hot error and render paths without changing the contract.
Cross-cutting stateless i18n functions (#307). Zero infrastructure types are re-exported; tr() runs on hot UI paths (115+ call sites) where wrapper indirection is pure overhead.
